distributionsVsOcf.title: Distributions from associates vs statutory operating cash flow
distributionsVsOcf.content:
ALX holds its largest asset -- a 30.8% stake in the APRR motorway group -- as an equity-accounted investment, not a consolidated subsidiary. Under IFRS, cash actually received from APRR and Chicago Skyway is classified as an investing cash flow (a return of/on investment), not an operating one, even though it is the cash that funds ALX's distributions to securityholders.

For Atlas Arteria: FY2025 distributions received from associates were A$516.8m versus statutory operating cash flow of just A$88.2m -- the statutory OCF line captures only the wholly/majority-owned toll roads (Dulles Greenway, Chicago Skyway consolidated revenue, Warnow) and misses the dominant APRR cash stream entirely. The DCF's owner-FCF base is built from this distributions series, not from OperatingCashFlow.

What to watch:

  • Distributions trending with APRR's underlying toll revenue and French tax changes, not with statutory OCF
  • A widening or narrowing gap as APRR's payout ratio or the ownership stake changes
  • Chicago Skyway and CCPI loan interest are the other (smaller) components of this line

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Atlas Arteria: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Atlas Arteria: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Atlas Arteria: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF here is statutory operating cash flow less capex, but for a holdco whose main asset is equity-accounted, that line excludes the cash ALX actually receives from APRR and Chicago Skyway. Owner FCF (from the DCF) is instead built from distributions received from associates plus consolidated toll cash flows, less corporate costs and tax -- the cash available to fund distributions to securityholders.

For Atlas Arteria: FY2025 owner FCF (A$474.4m) is roughly 5x reported statutory FCF (A$87.6m) -- the gap is the APRR/Skyway distributions booked in investing activities, not an earnings-quality problem.

What to watch:

  • Owner FCF versus the distributions-from-associates series (Equity-Accounted Economics section above), not versus net income
  • Company-reported "Operating free cash flow" (A$505.9m, 34.9cps FY2025) as the closest non-IFRS analogue

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Atlas Arteria: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Atlas Arteria: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Atlas Arteria: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue here is statutory consolidated toll revenue -- Dulles Greenway, Chicago Skyway and Warnow Tunnel only.

For Atlas Arteria: this line captures under 15% of the business's economics. The 30.8% APRR stake (~83% of proportional toll revenue, A$2,012.3m proportionate FY2025) is equity-accounted and never appears here -- it shows up instead as "share of associate profit" in net income and as distributions received in investing cash flow. Statutory revenue growth is not a useful proxy for ALX's underlying growth.

What to watch:

  • Proportional/proportionate KPIs (toll revenue, EBITDA) that management discloses alongside statutory figures
  • APRR toll escalation and French traffic/tax developments, which drive the bulk of value

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Atlas Arteria: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.growth_hint: Contractual toll escalation + ~1% APRR traffic growth
dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — distributions from APRR/Skyway + consolidated tolls, less corporate costs & tax
